title: Claude AI can plug directly into your bank account
summary:
Anthropic has a new pitch for managing your personal finances: let Claude do it instead, with a new Personal Finance feature that connects it to your bank and card accounts via the Plaid bank bridging platform.
Its access is read-only, and with Plaid facilitating the connection, Claude doesn’t see your banking passwords and your bank doesn’t have to deal with unvetted AI bots crawling around your accounts.
Personal Finance in Claude is rolling out in beta this week to Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plan subscribers in the US.
Anthropic’s announcement follows OpenAI introducing a similar feature for ChatGPT in May, which also plugs into your bank accounts through Plaid.
For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust.

summary:
At an elite gathering of investors on Wednesday, some of the juiciest conversations were about the outlook for AI, job creation and destruction, and Elon Musk's vision of the future.
Across the day, however, three topics dominated: the ongoing AI bubble debate, how the job market will develop as AI grows, and the world's richest man, Elon Musk.

title: Apple's Insider Trading Policy Now Covers Prediction Markets
summary:
Apple has added an explicit ban on using confidential information to bet on prediction markets to its insider trading policy, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The new version is marked "Updated October 2026," while an earlier version that Apple filed in 2024 doesn't mention prediction markets at all.
If you haven't heard of them, prediction markets are basically platforms where people buy and sell contracts that pay out depending on whether a future event happens.
Apple also says employees must not share confidential information to others who may go on to use it on such markets.
Apple's insider trading policy applies to directors, officers, employees, independent contractors and consultants, as well as to family members who live with them or are financially dependent on them.

title: Claude Gets Personal Finance Feature With Bank Account Linking
summary:
Anthropic today added Personal Finance to Claude, allowing users to connect their bank and card accounts for analysis.
Claude has access to the bank name, account name and type, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions for bank accounts.
Personal Finance chats are not used for model training and are not added to Claude's shared memory.
OpenAI added a similar finance feature to ChatGPT back in May.
Personal Finance is rolling out in beta on the Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in the United States.

Democrats’ recent messaging has promised a Big Tech and AI crackdown.

title: OpenAI says its new cybersecurity model is better at not hacking other companies
summary:
OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber, the latest version of its cybersecurity AI model, which it says is better at finding vulnerabilities and less likely to go rogue and hack other platforms in the process.
OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber.
Following a wave of AI cybersecurity incidents, OpenAI has raced to strengthen its safeguards and lock down its most powerful models.
The company briefly paused training of its frontier AI models, and it now restricts their access to the internet.
Additionally, GPT-6 Cyber comes with stronger safeguards “to detect and disrupt misuse” while better adhering to user instructions.

title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
summary:
Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents.
The startup’s new always-on “Teammates” can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.
Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks.

title: Google Is Forcing AI Overviews in Classrooms. Schools Are Searching for a Way Out
summary:
Two weeks ago, an IT administrator for an elementary-middle school took to Google’s support forums requesting a way to block students from seeing AI Overviews—the chatbot-generated answers at the top of search results.
But counterparts from three districts voiced similar frustration and pointed to work-arounds they were employing or considering to block AI Overviews in lieu of an official “off” switch.
Google announced on Tuesday that it is declining to provide schools an option to disable AI Overviews.
Instead, starting next year, schools will have to block access to search altogether to get rid of the feature.
The issue for schools and parents, though, is that Google considers AI Overviews and a companion feature called AI Mode inseparable from the traditional search experience.

The AI-generated sci-fi film Gods Don’t Give Gifts has added a bit of star power: Pop star Grimes is going to appear in the movie.
Billed as “the first AI film to come to theatres,” Gods Don’t Give Gifts is a notable test case for the commercial potential of AI films, and it releases on December 4th.

title: AI teddy makes unprompted 'I can't help with killing you' remark
summary:
An AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question.
It came amid a BBC investigation into AI toys and it made the unprompted remark while being asked how babies are made.
AI toy company founder Paul Clarke said the industry was "crying out" for regulation - a call echoed by the children's commissioner for Wales.
The UK government said children's safety would always be a top priority and it supported innovation while ensuring products were safe.
Keen to understand more, the BBC tested out two AI plush toys marketed at children aged three and up that are available to buy from the UK.

SpaceX is teaming up with Qualcomm to build out its nationwide mobile network.

title: Uber only fulfilled 4 rides from AI agents last quarter
summary:
AI agents won’t be stealing Uber’s lunch any time soon.
Only four rides were arranged by third-party AI agents during the third quarter of 2026, Uber executives disclosed during an earnings call this morning.
The volume of Uber Eats orders fulfilled by AI agents was a little higher, with the company recording “around 500” during the week of Halloween, out of a total 320 million Uber rides and Uber Eats deliveries.
This is the first time that Uber has disclosed the number of third-party AI agents that have arranged deliveries or rides on its platform.
With the rise of AI agents like Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots, some experts are predicting that platforms like Uber and DoorDash are at risk of disintermediation, in which customers use AI agents to order food or book a ride, rather than visiting the app itself.

“Today’s AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment,” Airbnb said.

title: VC firm Sequoia is flattening its partner structure and closing its London office
summary:
At Sequoia Capital, London is out, and the Great Flattening is in.
The Silicon Valley VC firm said Wednesday it has made internal changes to undo a management hierarchy that had "crept over into the investing team."
The VC firm, which made early-stage bets on companies such as Apple, Google, and Nvidia, said it can support European founders and startups from its Bay Area headquarters.
By closing its London office, winding down programs for early founders, and flattening its investing partnership, Sequoia is betting that a leaner structure will help it double down on concentrated, founder-led decision-making.
The VC firm is also dropping its Monday partner meeting cycle, and said that its mission of delivering the best possible returns to limited partners remains the same.

title: OpenAI lays out new policy framework for data centers
summary:
OpenAI has backed a new set of measures the company says will give communities a greater say in data center development, according to a policy announcement shared with POLITICO.
The framework shows how one of the world's leading artificial intelligence labs is attempting to reconcile public opposition to the infrastructure with Silicon Valley's need to keep building data centers to support artificial intelligence development.
It would also allow providers to throttle power to data centers during periods of high demand.
OpenAI also unveiled new commitments to communities near its data centers, including a promise to pay for the full cost of energy usage and infrastructure, prioritize closed-loop cooling systems that use less water and work with local unions to fill jobs at the data centers.
They also announced plans to rebrand data centers as "compute campuses," an apparent acknowledgement of the widespread public dislike for the infrastructure's longtime name.

title: AMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in history
summary:
AMD CEO Lisa Su said in the company’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that Q3 2026 was “was the largest and most profitable in our history.” AMD reported a record $13.4 billion in quarterly revenue, and it’s predicting it will hit another record high next quarter of $17 billion.
The company’s data center business is driving that growth, with $8.5 billion in data center quarterly revenue for Q3 2026.
Su said AMD’s expecting its revenue to “grow more than 80 percent in 2027,” adding that “data center will be the largest contributor.”Eventually, most of AMD’s revenue might come from its data center business.
Over the last couple years, jumps in the company’s revenue have been closely mirroring its data center business — in Q3 2026 its overall revenue went up $1.9 billion, while its data center revenue went up $1.8 billion.
As AMD keeps smashing its data center revenue records, its gaming business dropped 40 percent compared to last year, dipping to $773 million.

title: Elon Musk's Gas-Powered xAI Data Centers Are Running Into A Big Problem With Locals
summary:
Elon Musk, the momentary trillionaire, has been under fire over his company, xAI, and its use of gas turbines to power data centers.
In Boxtown, Memphis, the NAACP has accused Musk's xAI of disregarding safeguards due to it being an area with a large Black community.
It has also alleged that the gas turbines were put up illegally, without proper planning permission.
The NAACP has since taken xAI to court over turbines at its nearby Mississippi facility.
During 2025, xAI had 35 different turbines operating, removed some, and then replaced them with three larger turbines.
